expectations.text: Tests each platform against whether it reaches a segment the demand evidence names, not only against the stalled deal value
expectations.evidence: The transcript tests each platform only on stalled-deal value and cost. It asks for the $900K to be split "by platform, and by named deal" and says to "Pick the platform with more named stalled dollars." It also asks whether the badge or listing is the real blocker. It never asks whether Salesforce or NetSuite users match a customer segment that the demand evidence names. Even the 'named-deal evidence line' is framed as dollars and stage, not segment fit. Only the per-deal, per-platform breakdown comes close to the criterion.

expectations.evidence: The response asks to 'Split the $900K by platform. Which deals need NetSuite, and which need Salesforce? Build for the larger half first.' It also asks whether the badge/listing or the connector is the real blocker. This links each platform to the stalled deals, but the test is still sized by deal dollars. It never asks whether AppExchange or Built for NetSuite reaches a buyer segment named in the demand evidence, such as the industry, ERP/CRM stack, or company size of the stalled prospects, or whether those buyers find vendors through that marketplace.
